references.text: Here Israel's leaders are compared to buildings that look beautiful on the outside but are full of deceit and evil on the inside, similar to the description of the hypocritical scribes and Pharisees in Matthew.
Ezekiel warns against false prophets in Israel who resemble the hypocritical religious leaders Jesus mentions, appearing righteous outwardly but filled with injustice and wickedness inwardly.

Jesus warns against false prophets who come to the people in sheep's clothing, but inwardly are ravenous wolves, paralleling his description of scribes and Pharisees who appear righteous on the outside but are full of hypocrisy and evil on the inside.

In the same chapter as the verse, Jesus expands his criticism of the scribes and Pharisees by comparing them to whitewashed tombs that look beautiful on the outside but are full of death and uncleanness on the inside.
